reference.title: Scenario 2 — Multiple causes for one problem
reference.shortdesc: Consider a .docx document containing one condition followed by multiple causes and corresponding remedies.

section.p: Consider a .docx document containing one condition followed by multiple causes and corresponding remedies. The following example shows how the converter transforms this structure into a DITA <troubleshooting> topic.

row.entry: [Heading 2]: The Printer Does Not Print [Normal, Bold run: "Cause 1:"] Paper tray is empty. [Normal, Bold run: "Remedy:"] [List Number]: 1. Load paper into the paper tray. [Normal, Bold run: "Cause 2:"] Printer is offline. [Normal, Bold run: "Remedy:"] [List Number]: 1. Reconnect the printer to the network.

entry.codeblock:
The Printer Does Not Print Condition

The printer does not print.

 Cause 1

Paper tray is empty.

 Remedy Load paper. Cause 2

Printer is offline.

 Remedy Reconnect printer.

section.p: Result: Each cause-and-remedy pair produces its own <troubleSolution>, while the shared problem heading maps to a single <condition> at the top of <troublebody>.
